topic: Earthquake waves and Earth's interior layers
key_concepts: Earth's interior consists of crust, mantle, and core
Crust is the outermost solid rocky layer
Mantle is the thickest, semi-solid layer rich in iron, magnesium, and silicon
Outer core is liquid iron and nickel; inner core is a solid iron-nickel ball
Seismic waves are energy released by earthquakes
Body waves include P waves and S waves; surface waves are felt at the surface
P waves are longitudinal, fastest, and travel through solids, liquids, and gases
S waves are transverse, slower, and travel only through solids
Seismic wave speed changes with material and density, revealing Earth's internal structure
S waves cannot pass through the liquid outer core, creating a shadow zone
Surface waves are slowest and cause the most earthquake damage
P, S, and surface waves arrive in that order at seismic stations
